title: 26.3亿美元！辉瑞牵手星锐医药，拿下in vivo CAR-T海外独家权益
content: 首页 资讯 摩熵视野 交易并购 26.3亿美元！辉瑞牵手星锐医药，拿下in vivo CAR-T海外独家权益 26.3亿美元！辉瑞牵手星锐医药，拿下in vivo CAR-T海外独家权益 触界生物 15小时前 查看原文 115 CAR-T 新闻摘要2026年11月18日，辉瑞（纽交所代码：PFE）官宣与星锐医药（Starna Therapeutics）达成独家许可协议。星锐医药聚焦RNA药物开发，主打体内原位疗法技术平台。根据协议约定，辉瑞获得三款IND申报前阶段、针对自身免疫性疾病的in vivo CAR-T项目，在大中华区以外区域的独家开发、生产与商业化权益。合作范围不止三款候选产品。辉瑞同步取得星锐医药专有体内CAR-T技术在炎症免疫、肿瘤领域的使用权限，拥有后续合作中新候选化合物的独家授权选择权，并且保留将全部授权地域拓展至大中华区的权利。这笔交易，也成为国内RNA递送与体内细胞治疗赛道又一标志性出海授权案例。交易条款拆解本次合作财务结构清晰，星锐医药将先收获3.3亿美元首付款，后续可依据开发、注册、商业化节点，拿到最高23亿美元里程碑款项，产品成功上市后，还能按照净销售额获取分级特许权使用费。在权责划分上，辉瑞将主导大中华区以外的全部临床开发工作，初期临床试验制剂计划在美国自有设施完成生产，同时独家掌控海外市场商业化运营。地域选择权的设置，也为双方后续在中国市场的协同预留了弹性空间。整体交易对价上限达26.3亿美元，体现跨国药企对in vivo CAR-T技术方向以及星锐递送平台价值的认可。致力于开发肝外靶向的LNP药物递送系统解决RNA药物靶向和治疗需求传统CAR-T疗法需要采集患者T细胞，在体外完成基因编辑、扩增后回输，制备周期长、成本高昂，规模化普及难度大。而星锐医药的in vivo CAR-T路线依托自研RNA递送体系，直接把编码CAR的RNA递送到患者体内T细胞中，在体内原位生成CAR-T细胞，属于“现货型”细胞治疗新范式。这套方案依托其核心肝外靶向LNP平台，突破传统LNP容易富集在肝脏的局限，把RNA递送到目标免疫细胞，简化生产流程、降低治疗门槛，在自身免疫病场景具备独特潜力。自身免疫疾病长期缺少安全且长效的根治方案，也是辉瑞炎症免疫管线重点布局的方向，二者管线需求高度契合。三款IND申报前阶段、针对自身免疫性疾病的in vivo CAR-T项目管线本次合作对双方具备不同战略价值。对于辉瑞而言，这笔授权直接补齐其在体内CAR-T赛道的布局，扩充炎症与免疫学管线，为自免疾病、肿瘤领域储备差异化下一代疗法。对于星锐医药，合作是对其RNA靶向递送底层能力的权威验证，可以借力辉瑞在RNA药物、免疫学、全球临床开发、合规与商业化体系的成熟能力，加快管线推进速度，推动技术平台国际化。星锐医药的平台价值，也不止本次授权的三款自免管线。依托这套体内CAR-T底层技术，团队还可以持续衍生更多候选分子，覆盖炎症免疫与肿瘤等广阔适应症。在CGT、RNA疗法持续升温的产业周期下，这次合作也印证：具备自主可控递送技术、能够解决真实临床痛点的国内生物技术公司，正持续获得全球头部药企的青睐。会议名称：第二届体内细胞治疗创新峰会（IN VIVO 2027）主办单位：触界生物会议时间：2027年2月25-26号会议地点：苏州点击“阅读原文”报名参加IN VIVO 2027 title: DISCO, AbbVie Sign AND-Gated Bispecific Deal Worth Up to $2.5B
content: Advertisement News|Articles|November 19, 2026 DISCO, AbbVie Sign AND-Gated Bispecific Deal Worth Up to $2.5B Author(s)Pharmaceutical Executive Editorial Staff Listen0:00 / 0:00 Key Takeaways Financial economics reflect a platform-style structure: $40 million upfront versus up to $2.5 billion contingent milestones, with most consideration dependent on research success and option exercise decisions. DISCOtech® surfaceome mapping is used to nominate paired cell-surface antigens enriched on tumor cells to reduce on-target, off-tumor toxicity via an AND-gated mechanism. AND-gated constructs are intended to activate only when both targets co-occur on the same cell, supporting ADC and T-cell engager approaches in difficult solid tumors. Recent transactions, including an Amgen license and AbbVie’s other bispecific licensing, underscore sustained big-pharma interest in bispecific formats and risk-managed option-based deal structures. Key unknowns include target identities, program count, stage-specific payment breakdowns, royalty rates, and any supporting preclinical or clinical efficacy/safety data for the platform’s AND-gated claims.SHOW MORE DISCO Pharmaceuticals gets $40M upfront from AbbVie and could earn up to $2.5B in milestones to develop AND-gated bispecifics for solid tumors. Advertisement DISCO Pharmaceuticals and AbbVie have entered a strategic collaboration and option-to-license agreement to discover and develop AND-gated bispecific therapeutics for solid tumors with high unmet medical need.1 DISCO will receive $40 million in upfront payments and is eligible for up to $2.5 billion in option, development, and other milestone payments, plus tiered royalties on worldwide net sales.1“Our AND-gated approach is designed to selectively target tumor cells while sparing healthy tissue,” said Mark Manfredi, Ph.D., CEO of DISCO Pharmaceuticals.1 For AbbVie, the agreement adds access to early-stage targets in an area of oncology where distinguishing tumor cells from healthy tissue is a central design challenge.“This collaboration further underscores the potential of our differentiated platform.”— Ajla Hrle, Ph.D., chief business officer, DISCO PharmaceuticalsWhat are the financial terms of the DISCO-AbbVie bispecific deal?The structure is common in platform-based partnerships: a modest upfront payment paired with a much larger pool of contingent milestones. The $40 million upfront payment is less than 2% of the up to $2.5 billion in potential payments, so most of the headline value depends on research outcomes and on AbbVie exercising its options.1 Under the agreement, DISCO will complete specified research activities, after which AbbVie may exclusively license selected programs.1The collaboration pairs DISCO’s DISCOtech® surfaceome mapping platform and its AND-gated discovery approach with AbbVie’s oncology research and development expertise.1 The portions of the release reviewed do not break out payments by stage, the number of programs, or royalty rates.How does DISCO's DISCOtech platform identify tumor-selective targets?DISCO says its DISCOtech platform maps cancer-specific cell-surface expression to identify pairs of targets, with the aim of reducing on-target, off-tumor toxicity.1 That type of toxicity arises when a drug engages a target that is also present on healthy tissue. As the term is generally used, an AND-gated therapeutic is intended to act only when both members of a target pair appear on the same cell, a pattern the company aims to find in tumor cells but not in normal ones. Manfredi said the platform’s ability to identify tumor-selective target pairs supports therapies with a potentially wider therapeutic window.1 (()=>{var l=(n,t)=>{let i=async()=>{await(await n())()},e=typeof t.value=="object"?t.value:void 0,s={timeout:e==null?void 0:e.timeout};"requestIdleCallback"in window?window.requestIdleCallback(i,s):setTimeout(i,s.timeout||200)};(self.Astro||(self.Astro={})).idle=l;window.dispatchEvent(new Event("astro:idle"));})(); The company develops AND-gated antibody-drug conjugates and T-cell engagers for hard-to-treat tumors, and its lead programs, directed at small cell lung cancer and colorectal cancer, are progressing toward the clinic.1How does the agreement fit into each company’s recent dealmaking?The agreement follows an earlier 2026 transaction. In January, DISCO announced an exclusive license with Amgen for a cancer target mapped on the cell surface by its platform, with potential total deal value of up to $618 million plus royalties.2 Ajla Hrle, Ph.D., DISCO’s chief business officer, said the AbbVie collaboration complements the company’s internal and partnered pipeline.1 AbbVie, for its part, announced an exclusive licensing agreement in January to develop a novel bispecific antibody for advanced solid tumors.3 Taken together, the transactions suggest continued interest from large drugmakers in bispecific formats for solid tumors. Option-based structures such as the DISCO agreement also let a larger company limit upfront spending while keeping the right to advance programs that mature. The available documents do not describe how AbbVie would prioritize the DISCO programs against its existing assets.What is still unknown about the collaboration?No clinical data accompany the announcement. The collaboration programs are at the research stage, since DISCO must complete specified research activities before AbbVie can exercise its option.1 The milestone figures are potential payments, not committed revenue, and the portions of the release reviewed do not identify the targets or specific tumor types involved. Because DISCO’s lead programs have not entered the clinic, no peer-reviewed publications or trial registry entries were identified to support efficacy or safety claims for the AND-gated approach, and none are cited here. The next milestones to watch are completion of DISCO’s research activities and AbbVie’s decisions on which programs to license.SourcesDISCO Pharmaceuticals announces strategic collaboration with AbbVie to advance next-generation AND-gated bispecific therapeutics for solid tumors. title: STAT Plus: Merck, Isomorphic Labs partner to develop oncology drug candidates
content: STAT PlusExclusive Merck, Isomorphic Labs partner to develop oncology drug candidates Collaboration will focus on small molecules aimed at undisclosed oncology target Manage alerts for this article Save this story for later Share this article Adobe By Katherine MacPhailNov. 19, 2026 Reporter, Live Journalism Katherine MacPhail[email protected]Katherine MacPhail is a reporter and editorial events programmer for STAT. Merck and Isomorphic Labs, the artificial intelligence drug designer built on a Nobel winning technology that can model how molecules will bind to proteins, said Thursday that they are entering into a research collaboration to discover small molecule candidates for an undisclosed oncology target of “strategic importance.” The partnership — only the latest such deal between a pharma giant and Isomorphic — will bring together the latter’s proprietary drug design engine and existing wet lab data from Merck, officials from both companies said. Merck will handle the preclinical and clinical development, manufacturing, and commercializing of any products. Advertisement “It is a target of high interest to us, a target where we have deployed internal efforts, and we think the pairing of those datasets with the Isomorphic drug discovery engine technology could be a very powerful pairing,” said George Addona, global head of discovery, preclinical development, and translational medicine at Merck. He is also the author of the morning Pharmalittle newsletter and the afternoon Pharmalot newsletter. Rise and shine, everyone, another busy day is on the way. And it is getting off to a pleasant start here on the Pharmalot campus, where clear blue skies and comfy breezes are greeting us. As for the official mascots, they have finished keeping passersby at bay and are now happily snoozing in their respective corners. As for us, we are firing up the trusty kettle for another cup of stimulation. Our choice today is peppermint, an old standby from our pantry. Of course, you are invited to join us. Meanwhile, here is the latest menu of tidbits. As always, do keep in touch. And best of luck today. … Merck and Isomorphic Labs, the artificial intelligence drug designer built on a Nobel-winning technology that can model how molecules will bind to proteins, are entering into a research collaboration to discover small molecule candidates for an undisclosed oncology target of “strategic importance,” STAT reports. The partnership — only the latest such deal between a pharma giant and Isomorphic — will join Isomorphic’s proprietary drug design engine and existing wet lab data from Merck, which will handle the preclinical and clinical development, manufacturing, and commercializing of any products. Advertisement The U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved a Sanofi drug, making ​it the first treatment for a ‌type of rare genetic condition that affects the brain and nervous system, Reuters writes. The drug, ​branded as Infilbray, was approved for ​adults and children weighing at least ⁠15 kilograms, or about 33 pounds, ​with type 3 Gaucher disease, a ​rare inherited disorder that causes fatty substances to build up in the body and brain. The ​approval was based on a late-stage ​study of 43 patients aged 12 years and ‌older ⁠whose symptoms outside the brain and nervous system had been stabilized with enzyme replacement therapy. content: EX-99.1 2 ef20084500_ex99-1.htm EXHIBIT 99.1 Exhibit 99.1 Insmed Reports Third-Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Provides Business Update —Total Company Revenues of $524.4 Million for the Third Quarter of 2026— —BRINSUPRI® (brensocatib) Revenues of $400.1 Million for the Third Quarter of 2026, Reflecting 29% Growth Over the Second Quarter of 2026— —ARIKAYCE® (amikacin liposome inhalation suspension) Revenues of $124.4 Million for the Third Quarter of 2026, Reflecting 9% Growth Over the Third Quarter of 2025— —Company Raises 2026 BRINSUPRI Revenue Guidance to $1.35 Billion to $1.4 Billion— —Company Raises 2026 ARIKAYCE Revenue Guidance to $460 Million to $470 Million— — Insmed Launches BRINSUPRI Tablets 25 mg (brensocatib hydrate) for the Treatment of Non-Cystic Fibrosis Bronchiectasis in Japan— BRIDGEWATER, N.J., October 29, 2026 — Insmed Incorporated (Nasdaq: INSM), a people-first global biopharmaceutical company striving to deliver first- and best-in-class therapies to transform the lives of patients facing serious diseases, today reported financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026, and provided a business update. “The third quarter marked another period of meaningful progress, defined by commercial momentum, regulatory achievements, and advancement across our diversified pipeline,” said Will Lewis, Chair and Chief Executive Officer of Insmed. “BRINSUPRI’s U.S. launch continues to exceed expectations and ARIKAYCE continues to grow while in its ninth year on the market. This performance supports our decision to raise the low end of our full-year 2026 revenue guidance for both products. We were also pleased to receive regulatory approval and launch BRINSUPRI in Japan, a profound milestone for patients living with bronchiectasis. In addition, the FDA’s acceptance of the sNDA for ARIKAYCE in MAC lung disease represents an important step toward expanding access to this therapy for eligible patients, including those that are newly diagnosed or facing recurrent infections. As we advance our Phase 3 TPIP programs across four large indications and progress our early-stage pipeline, we remain focused on delivering meaningful innovation and improving the lives of patients with serious diseases.” Progress and Anticipated Milestones by Therapeutic Area: Respiratory BRINSUPRI • BRINSUPRI global revenue grew 29% in the third quarter of 2026 compared to the second quarter of 2026, driven by strong growth in the U.S. market. • In August 2026, Japan's Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare (MHLW) approved BRINSUPRI Tablets 25 mg (brensocatib hydrate) for the treatment of non-cystic fibrosis bronchiectasis (NCFB) in adults and pediatric patients 12 years and older. • In October 2026, Insmed launched BRINSUPRI Tablets 25 mg, the first and only MHLW-approved treatment for NCFB, in Japan. 1 ARIKAYCE • ARIKAYCE global revenue grew 9% in the third quarter of 2026 compared to the third quarter of 2025, primarily driven by strong growth in international markets. • In September 2026, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) accepted Insmed’s Supplemental New Drug Application (sNDA) for review of ARIKAYCE for the treatment of Mycobacterium avium complex (MAC) lung disease as part of a combination antibacterial drug regimen. The FDA granted Priority Review to the sNDA and set a target action date of January 28, 2027, under the Prescription Drug User Fee Act (PDUFA). • Insmed plans to submit data from the Phase 3 ENCORE study to Japan’s Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Agency (PMDA) in the fourth quarter of 2026 to support potential ARIKAYCE label expansion to all patients with MAC lung disease. TPIP • Insmed has now enrolled more than 35% of patients in the Phase 3 PALM-ILD study of treprostinil palmitil inhalation powder (TPIP) in patients with pulmonary hypertension associated with interstitial lung disease (PH-ILD) and expects to complete enrollment in the first half of 2028. • In July 2026, Insmed enrolled its first patient in the Phase 3 PALM-PAH study of TPIP in patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH). • In September 2026, Insmed initiated the Phase 3 PALM-PPF study of TPIP in patients with progressive pulmonary fibrosis (PPF). • Insmed continues to anticipate initiating a Phase 3 study of TPIP in patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) in the first half of 2027. INS1148 • Insmed continues to advance a Phase 2 development program for INS1148, initially targeting IPF, with plans to evaluate PPF and other diseases where inhibition of the pro-inflammatory and pro-fibrotic responses mediated by stem cell factor 248 (SCF248) may be beneficial. Immunology & Inflammation INS1033 • In September 2026, the Phase 1 study of INS1033, a dipeptidyl peptidase 1 (DPP1) inhibitor cleared by the FDA for patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA), began active enrollment of healthy volunteers. Neuro & Other Rare INS1201 • Insmed completed enrollment of the Phase 1 ASCEND clinical study of INS1201, an intrathecally delivered gene therapy for patients with Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD). INS1202 • Insmed continues to enroll patients in the Phase 1 ARMOR study of INS1202, an intrathecally delivered gene therapy for patients with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). 2 Corporate Updates • In September 2026, Insmed presented five abstracts from across its Respiratory therapeutic area at the European Respiratory Society (ERS) Congress 2026. • In October 2026, Insmed presented data across its respiratory portfolio at the American College of Chest Physicians (CHEST) 2026 Annual Meeting and IDWeek 2026. • In October 2026, Insmed announced the appointment of Paul Hudson, former Chief Executive Officer of Sanofi and Novartis Pharmaceuticals, and Utpal Koppikar, current Chief Financial Officer of Verily Health, to its Board of Directors. Third-Quarter 2026 Financial Results The following table summarizes third-quarter and year-to-date 2026 and 2025 revenues and revenue growth for BRINSUPRI and ARIKAYCE across our commercial regions: INSMED INCORPORATED Revenue by Region (in millions) Three Months Ended September 30, Nine Months Ended September 30, (in millions) 2026 2025 Growth 2026 2025 Growth ARIKAYCE U.S. $ 75.5 $ 74.0 2% $ 208.6 $ 206.9 1% International 48.9 40.3 21% 130.2 107.6 21% Total $ 124.4 $ 114.3 9% $ 338.8 $ 314.5 8% BRINSUPRI U.S. $ 398.1 $ 28.1 NM $ 913.8 $ 28.1 NM International 2.0 - N/A 3.3 - N/A Total $ 400.1 $ 28.1 NM $ 917.1 $ 28.1 NM Total Revenues U.S. $ 473.6 $ 102.0 364% $ 1,122.4 $ 235.0 378% International 50.8 40.3 26% 133.5 107.6 24% Total $ 524.4 $ 142.3 268% $ 1,255.9 $ 342.6 267% • Cost of product revenues (excluding amortization of intangibles) were $78.2 million for the third quarter of 2026, compared to $29.4 million for the third quarter of 2025. The increase in cost of product revenues in the third quarter of 2026 primarily reflects the increase in total product revenues for ARIKAYCE and BRINSUPRI. Cost of product revenues as a percentage of revenues decreased in the third quarter of 2026 due to sales of BRINSUPRI, which has lower manufacturing costs than ARIKAYCE. • Research and development (R&D) expenses were $270.0 million for the third quarter of 2026, compared to $186.4 million for the third quarter of 2025. The increase in R&D expenses for the third quarter of 2026 was related to an increase in manufacturing costs, an increase in clinical development and research costs, both primarily related to TPIP, and an increase in compensation and benefit-related expenses and stock-based compensation costs due primarily to an increase in headcount. • Selling, general and administrative (SG&A) expenses for the third quarter of 2026 were $253.0 million, compared to $186.4 million for the third quarter of 2025. The increase in SG&A expenses for the third quarter of 2026 was primarily related to increases in professional fees and other external expenses, and an increase in compensation and benefit-related expenses due to an increase in headcount, both driven by commercial activities for BRINSUPRI. • For the third quarter of 2026, Insmed reported a net loss of $100.3 million, or $0.46 per share, compared to a net loss of $370.0 million, or $1.75 per share, for the third quarter of 2025. 3 Balance Sheet, Financial Guidance, and Planned Investments • As of September 30, 2026, Insmed had cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaling approximately $1.1 billion. • The Company raised its full-year 2026 revenue guidance for BRINSUPRI to a range of $1.35 billion to $1.4 billion from the previous guidance of $1.25 billion to $1.4 billion. • The Company raised its full-year 2026 revenue guidance for ARIKAYCE to a range of $460 million to $470 million from the previous guidance of $450 million to $470 million. • The Company continues to anticipate peak revenues for BRINSUPRI to be more than $7 billion, TPIP to be more than $6 billion, and ARIKAYCE to be more than $1 billion. • The Company continues to an
